verdict.rationale: cubic's AI wiki automatically indexes the whole codebase and produces searchable wikis with source links and architecture diagrams, so mapping and explaining a repo does not require hand-picking context files. Its MCP server also exposes codebase context to coding agents. However, the documented interactive chat is PR-centric and starts from selected code, and the wiki is described only briefly with no hands-on validation. Missing for 10: interactive agent Q&A over the whole unfamiliar codebase, in-depth docs on wiki coverage and quality, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent map and explain an entire unfamiliar codebase without manually selecting context files

citations.quote: cubic's AI wiki automatically indexes your codebase and produces searchable wikis, complete with links to source code, architecture diagrams, and more.
cubic exports the wiki as markdown files into a directory in your repo (default `.cubic/wiki`) and keeps them current through a rolling pull request.
Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context
